title: Suffolk could close 3 mobiles, Wiltshire first volunteer library starts
author: Ian Anstice / The Library Campaign

editorial.text: Please sign the national petition in support of public libraries. 422 libraries (337 buildings and 85 mobiles) currently under threat or closed/left council control since 1/4/11 out of c.4612 in the UK, complete list below. Librarian professional body CILIP forecasts 600 libraries under threat (inc. 20% of English libraries). The Public Libraries News figure is obtained from counting up all reports about public libraries in the media each day. News Award-winning Alan Bennett on how we need to safeguard our libraries for future generations – Mirror. “Municipal authorities of all parties point to splendid new and scheduled central libraries as if this discharges them of their obligations. It doesn’t. For a child, a library needs to be round the corner. And if we lose local libraries it is children who will suffer.” “We Love Libraries” image by justgrimes Taken from CPD23 Thing 16 – Walk You Home I love libraries because of the serendipitous searching experience … – Voices for the Library (Tumblr). “Essentially, I’d be lost without my local library.” Poems are the original text messages: Carol Ann Duffy on how to get children reading more poetry – Manchester Evening News. Interview with Poet Laureate. “Carol Ann Duffy is very cross. The Poet Laureate is angry about the threat to many of our libraries. “It’s awful,” she says. “I hope when this temporary coalition is not in office that it might be reversed by another government.” …”Carol Ann’s spent the last year joining protests against library closures. She believes libraries are an effective way of introducing young people to the world of reading and writing, something she is passionate about. And for the Poet Laureate, it’s personal. She says without access to a library when she was younger she wouldn’t be where she is today.”
